title: Can Data Work be Reparative?
title_zh: 数据工作能否具有修复性？
abstract_en: We present an ethnographic study of an alternative approach to data work, developed by a civic-tech initiative that builds datasets for training and benchmarking online safety systems. They aim to respond to online safety concerns from a feminist perspective, by building safety datasets collaboratively with those most impacted by online harms. In this paper, we examine how this approach aims to reorient data work as a site for repair and redress, and trace the struggles they encounter in the process. Specifically, we draw attention to the challenges and tensions involved in advancing just reward for data work and collective governance of AI datasets. Examining these challenges through an STS-informed lens of reparative justice and repair, we argue that the work of repairing data work (and AI) lies, fundamentally, in resetting the ties of accountability. At a time heightened emphasis on efforts like safety evaluations and red teaming to make AI more responsible, we highlight the need to confront foundational questions about how the humans involved in these efforts relate to the datasets and systems they help produce. A reparative lens demands that we interrupt prevailing norms of data work and place at their centre, not AI or datasets, but those most harmed by the neglect, oversight and exclusion animated in the current modes of dataset production. This, we argue, offers a bold vision for responsibility and contributes towards a critical agenda for building alternative futures of data and AI practice.
abstract_zh: 本文对一种替代性数据工作方式进行了民族志研究：一个 civic-tech initiative 为训练和评测 online safety systems 构建数据集，并试图从 feminist perspective 出发，邀请最受 online harms 影响的人共同参与安全数据集建设。论文考察了这一实践如何将数据工作重新定位为修复与补偿（repair and redress）的场域，并追踪其在推进过程中遭遇的困难。作者重点分析了数据工作的公正报酬（just reward）与 AI datasets 的集体治理（collective governance）之间的挑战和张力。借助 STS 视角下的 reparative justice 与 repair 理论，论文指出，修复数据工作乃至 AI 的核心，在于重置问责关系（ties of accountability）。在安全评测、red teaming 等负责任 AI 实践日益受到重视的背景下，作者强调必须直面一个基础问题：参与这些工作的个体如何与他们帮助生产的数据集和系统发生关系。修复性视角要求打断既有数据生产规范，将最受当前数据集生产模式中的忽视、遗漏与排斥所伤害的人置于中心，而非将 AI 或数据集本身置于中心。
key_points_zh: 论文基于 ethnographic study，研究一个 civic-tech initiative 如何协作构建 online safety datasets，用于训练和评测 online safety systems。
该项目从 feminist perspective 出发，强调让最受 online harms 影响的群体参与数据集建设，将数据工作视为 repair and redress 的场域。
作者指出，实现修复性数据工作面临两类核心张力：数据劳动的公正报酬，以及 AI datasets 的集体治理。
通过 STS-informed 的 reparative justice 视角，论文认为修复 AI 与数据工作的关键不是优化数据集本身，而是重置人、数据集与系统之间的问责关系。
论文对当前 safety evaluations、red teaming 等负责任 AI 实践提出批判性提醒：应把受伤害群体置于中心，而不是继续以 AI 系统或数据资产为中心。

llm_assessment.comment: The paper raises important sociotechnical governance issues around dataset labor, but has minimal direct relevance to agent runtime infrastructure or self-improving agent platforms.
